en.greeting: Hi! Today we work on whole sentences: which words are strong, how words join together, and how to keep the English beat. Say everything out loud, and clap along when we count beats.

steps.title: Strong words, weak words
steps.text: In a sentence, some words are strong and some are weak. Tap the words and listen.
steps.body: **Content words** carry the meaning: nouns (*bank, Rina*), main verbs (*work, buy*), adjectives (*new*), question words (*where*) and **not** (*can't, don't*). They are **stressed**: louder, longer, higher. **Function words** are the small glue words: *a, the, to, of, in, at, is, I, my*. They are **weak** and quick. Indonesian gives every word the same strength; English doesn't: *I WANT to GO to the SHOP*.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dimas is at work. Find the strong words.

question.prompt: Which words are strong in 'Dimas is at the office'?
question.explanation: **Dimas** (a name) and **office** (a noun) carry the meaning: *DI-mas is at the OF-fice*. **is**, **at** and **the** are function words, so they're weak. Giving every word the same strength is the Indonesian habit.

steps.title: Stress in sentences
steps.text: Listen and repeat. Make only the content words strong.
steps.body: Strong words: DI-mas WANTS NEW PHONE · WHERE BUS STA-tion · BU-di CAN'T COME to-DAY · SWIM (can is weak: 'kən') · O-pen WIN-dow. A small word at the end is said in full: *Yes, I CAN.*

examples.id: Budi tidak bisa datang hari ini.

steps.title: Linking: tur-noff
steps.text: English speakers don't stop between words. Tap and listen to how the words join.
steps.body: When a word **ends in a consonant sound** (huruf mati: n, k, t…) and the next word **starts with a vowel sound** (a, e, i, o, u), the consonant moves over: *turn off* → 'tur-noff', *an apple* → 'a-napple'. Listen to the **sound**, not the letter: *make it* = 'ma-kit' (the e is silent), *an hour* = 'a-nour' (the h is silent). The **-ed** links too: 'clean-dit'. Don't put a little stop before the vowel: not *an | apple*.

steps.title: Which one links?
steps.text: Look for a consonant sound followed by a vowel sound.

question.prompt: In which phrase does the last sound of the first word join the next word?
question.explanation: **an egg**: *an* ends in an **n** sound and *egg* starts with a vowel, so they link: 'a-negg'. *a banana*: *a* ends in a vowel sound. *big bag*: g and b are both consonants, so nothing moves.

steps.title: Listen: one word or two?
steps.text: Press play. Bu Ani is at the door of the classroom.

question.prompt: Listen. What does Bu Ani say?
question.explanation: You heard **Please come in.** (Silakan masuk.) *come* ends in **m** and *in* starts with a vowel, so they link: 'co-min'. It sounds almost like *coming*, but *Please coming* isn't correct English. *come on* has an 'o' sound, not 'i'.

steps.title: Keep the beat
steps.text: Clap once on each strong word. Tap each line and clap along.
steps.body: In Indonesian every syllable gets about the same time: *sa-ya-mau-ke-pa-sar*. In English the **strong words** come at roughly **regular** beats, and the weak words between them are **squeezed**: said faster and quieter. So *ONE and a TWO and a THREE* still has **3 claps**, and *RI-na is COOK-ing the RICE* has 3 beats, like *RI-na COOKS RICE*. Count the content words to count the beats.

steps.title: Fix the rhythm
steps.text: Pak Hasan is talking about his son. Help him sound natural.

question.prompt: Pak Hasan says 'My son is at school', giving every word the same time, like in Indonesian. How should it sound?
options: MY SON IS AT SCHOOL: 5 equal beats
my SON is at SCHOOL: 2 beats, small words squeezed
my son is at SCHOOL: 1 beat at the end
question.explanation: Only **son** and **school** are content words, so there are **2 beats**: *my SON is at SCHOOL*. *my*, *is* and *at* are squeezed between them. Five equal beats is the Indonesian rhythm, and one beat loses the word *son*.

steps.title: Build and say it
steps.text: Build the sentence, then say it with the strong words strong.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Sari mau secangkir teh.
question.solution: Sari wants a cup of tea.
question.explanation: Name first (**Sari**), then the verb (**wants**), then **a cup of tea**. Say it with 4 strong beats: *SA-ri WANTS a CUP of TEA*. **a** and **of** are weak and quick, and *cup_of* links: 'cu-pof'.

steps.text: Flip the cards and say each answer out loud.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita berlatih kalimat utuh: kata mana yang kuat, bagaimana kata-kata tersambung, dan cara menjaga ketukan bahasa Inggris. Ucapkan semuanya dengan suara keras, dan tepuk tangan saat kita menghitung ketukan.

steps.title: Kata kuat, kata lemah
steps.text: Dalam kalimat, ada kata yang kuat dan ada yang lemah. Ketuk kata-katanya dan dengarkan.
steps.body: **Kata isi** (content words) membawa arti: kata benda (*bank, Rina*), kata kerja utama (*work, buy*), kata sifat (*new*), kata tanya (*where*) dan **not** (*can't, don't*). Kata-kata ini **ditekan**: lebih keras, lebih panjang, lebih tinggi. **Kata tugas** (function words) adalah kata kecil perekat: *a, the, to, of, in, at, is, I, my*. Kata-kata ini **lemah** dan cepat. Bahasa Indonesia memberi setiap kata kekuatan yang sama; bahasa Inggris tidak: *I WANT to GO to the SHOP*.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dimas sedang di tempat kerja. Cari kata-kata yang kuat.

question.prompt: Kata mana yang kuat di 'Dimas is at the office'?
question.explanation: **Dimas** (nama) dan **office** (kata benda) membawa arti: *DI-mas is at the OF-fice*. **is**, **at** dan **the** adalah kata tugas, jadi lemah. Memberi semua kata kekuatan yang sama adalah kebiasaan dari bahasa Indonesia.

steps.title: Tekanan dalam kalimat
steps.text: Dengarkan dan tirukan. Buat hanya kata isinya yang kuat.
steps.body: Kata yang kuat: DI-mas WANTS NEW PHONE · WHERE BUS STA-tion · BU-di CAN'T COME to-DAY · SWIM (can lemah: 'ken') · O-pen WIN-dow. Kata kecil di akhir kalimat diucapkan utuh: *Yes, I CAN.*

examples.id: Budi tidak bisa datang hari ini.

steps.title: Linking: tur-noff
steps.text: Penutur bahasa Inggris tidak berhenti di antara kata. Ketuk dan dengarkan bagaimana kata-katanya tersambung.
steps.body: Kalau sebuah kata **berakhir dengan bunyi konsonan** (huruf mati: n, k, t…) dan kata berikutnya **diawali bunyi vokal** (a, e, i, o, u), konsonannya pindah: *turn off* → 'tur-noff', *an apple* → 'a-napple'. Dengarkan **bunyinya**, bukan hurufnya: *make it* = 'ma-kit' (e tidak dibaca), *an hour* = 'a-nour' (h tidak dibaca). Akhiran **-ed** juga tersambung: 'clean-dit'. Jangan buat hentakan kecil sebelum vokal: bukan *an | apple*.

steps.title: Mana yang tersambung?
steps.text: Cari bunyi konsonan yang diikuti bunyi vokal.

question.prompt: Di frasa mana bunyi terakhir kata pertama bergabung dengan kata berikutnya?
question.explanation: **an egg**: *an* berakhir bunyi **n** dan *egg* diawali vokal, jadi tersambung: 'a-negg'. *a banana*: *a* berakhir bunyi vokal. *big bag*: g dan b sama-sama konsonan, jadi tidak ada yang pindah.

steps.title: Dengar: satu kata atau dua?
steps.text: Tekan play. Bu Ani ada di pintu kelas.

question.prompt: Dengarkan. Apa yang Bu Ani katakan?
question.explanation: Kamu mendengar **Please come in.** (Silakan masuk.) *come* berakhir **m** dan *in* diawali vokal, jadi tersambung: 'co-min'. Terdengar hampir seperti *coming*, tapi *Please coming* bukan bahasa Inggris yang benar. *come on* berbunyi 'o', bukan 'i'.

steps.title: Jaga ketukannya
steps.text: Tepuk tangan sekali di setiap kata kuat. Ketuk setiap baris dan ikuti tepukannya.
steps.body: Dalam bahasa Indonesia setiap suku kata mendapat waktu yang kira-kira sama: *sa-ya-mau-ke-pa-sar*. Dalam bahasa Inggris **kata-kata kuat** datang dengan ketukan yang kurang lebih **teratur**, dan kata lemah di antaranya **diselipkan**: lebih cepat dan lebih pelan. Jadi *ONE and a TWO and a THREE* tetap **3 tepukan**, dan *RI-na is COOK-ing the RICE* punya 3 ketukan, sama seperti *RI-na COOKS RICE*. Hitung kata isinya untuk menghitung ketukan.

steps.title: Perbaiki ritmenya
steps.text: Pak Hasan sedang bercerita tentang anak laki-lakinya. Bantu dia terdengar alami.

question.prompt: Pak Hasan mengucapkan 'My son is at school' dengan waktu yang sama untuk setiap kata, seperti bahasa Indonesia. Seharusnya bagaimana?
options: MY SON IS AT SCHOOL: 5 equal beats
my SON is at SCHOOL: 2 beats, small words squeezed
my son is at SCHOOL: 1 beat at the end
question.explanation: Hanya **son** dan **school** yang kata isi, jadi ada **2 ketukan**: *my SON is at SCHOOL*. *my*, *is* dan *at* diselipkan di antaranya. Lima ketukan yang sama itu ritme bahasa Indonesia, dan satu ketukan saja menghilangkan kata *son*.
displayOptions: MY SON IS AT SCHOOL: 5 ketukan sama kuat
my SON is at SCHOOL: 2 ketukan, kata kecil diucapkan cepat
my son is at SCHOOL: 1 ketukan di akhir

steps.title: Susun dan ucapkan
steps.text: Susun kalimatnya, lalu ucapkan dengan kata-kata kuat yang benar-benar kuat.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Sari mau secangkir teh.
question.solution: Sari wants a cup of tea.
question.explanation: Nama dulu (**Sari**), lalu kata kerjanya (**wants**), lalu **a cup of tea**. Ucapkan dengan 4 ketukan kuat: *SA-ri WANTS a CUP of TEA*. **a** dan **of** lemah dan cepat, dan *cup_of* tersambung: 'cu-pof'.

steps.title: Kartu hafalan
steps.text: Balik kartunya dan ucapkan setiap jawaban dengan keras.
